author: refuter
body: Attacked the pass's affirmative result as stated ('about n^0.57 switches suffice for typical linear supply'). Two independent grounds, arithmetic against the exact on-disk column (code/out/threshold_limit_exact.txt), not a model search (asymptotic claim, not finitely falsifiable). (1) 0.57 is NOT a settled exponent or clean closed form. The run's own saturation theory (scholar_threshold_exact_mean.md) predicts log2(w) = L/2 + 0.42sqrt(L), slope = 1/2 + 0.21/sqrt(L). Against the exact w-column (3,3,3,4,3,5,7,11,16,24,35,52,77): last-3 slope mean = 0.5606 vs theory 0.561@L=12 — match to 0.000; last-7 mean 0.5635. The slope is a slow drift to 1/2, not a constant. The directive's only other candidate log_4(3)=0.7925 is refuted decisively (slope never leaves 0.54-0.57). Honest closed form: w ~ n^{1/2+o(1)} (sublinearly square-root, with subpolynomial correction). (2) The exact-mean column settles only the MEAN half of 'typical', which is defined as mean>=0.40 AND frac>=0.5. The sampled frac half (PART B, same capture) is marginal AT the crossing: at n=256 the exact-mean crossing is w=16 but frac(16) ~0.49 (frac 0.389@w=13, 0.579@w=19), so the two-condition theta* is w=19 not 16; at n=512 crossing w=24 but frac 0.528@w=26, theta* = 26 not 24. The true theta* sits ABOVE the exact-mean theta, so the 0.57 fit is built on the weaker of the two conditions. Both grounds leave the SUBLINEAR content intact (w ~ n^{1/2+o(1)}) and do NOT touch the primes' transfer (non-adversariality is still the whole open step). refs: threshold-mean-exact-parity-formula, code/out/threshold_limit_exact.txt
